own_solution.law: Snell's law n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2)

notes: Base: sin(theta2) = sin 40 / 1.5 = 0.64279/1.5 = 0.42853, theta2 = 25.37 deg. With the incoming ray tilted 10 deg farther from the normal, incidence 50 deg: sin(theta2) = 0.76604/1.5 = 0.51070, theta2 = 30.71 deg. Going from n=1 into n=1.5 there is no total internal reflection at any incidence. A tilted solar panel on the roof or a tilted picture frame has no optical path to this ray. All four sentences state 10 deg. T4986 additionally specifies 'within the same plane of incidence'; T4453 says only 'away from the normal', which I read as an in-plane increase of the incidence angle by 10 deg (the natural reading); a partly out-of-plane rotation would increase the incidence angle by less, but that reading is strained. Not flagged.
